jobs.description:
Description

ProgressionLIVE développe des logiciels web et mobiles de gestion des opérations de service sur le terrain, utilisés par des centaines d’organisations canadiennes dans les secteurs du CVC, de la plomberie, de l’électricité, de la construction, du transport et de la maintenance.

Votre rôle

Relevant du directeur général, vous dirigerez toute l’équipe produit et technologie et serez responsable de la feuille de route et de la livraison. Vous définirez avec le directeur général les orientations produit, les priorités majeures et les investissements structurants, tout en exerçant votre autonomie sur les décisions courantes et l’exécution.

Vous combinerez jugement produit, leadership et contribution technique directe : accompagner les développeurs, renforcer leurs compétences avec l’IA et programmer certaines fonctionnalités jusqu’à leur mise en production. Vous vous appuierez sur les expertises de l’équipe pour les décisions techniques spécialisées.

Vos responsabilités

Piloter la feuille de route à partir des échanges clients, des données d’utilisation et des objectifs commerciaux. Collaborer avec les ventes et le service client, puis mesurer l’adoption et l’impact.
Diriger l’exécution : définir la portée, organiser les priorités, lever les obstacles et accompagner l’équipe jusqu’à la mise en production et à la validation des résultats.
Programmer et livrer certaines fonctionnalités, en respectant les exigences de tests, de revue de code et de sécurité. Créer aussi des prototypes et des outils internes.
Recruter et développer l’équipe. Accompagner les développeurs par le travail en binôme, les revues de code, la formation et le partage des connaissances.
Définir et diriger un modèle opérationnel activé par l’IA pour le produit et l’ingénierie. Habiliter les développeurs, l’assurance qualité et les DevOps à utiliser l’IA efficacement tout au long du cycle de vie du développement, de la recherche et des spécifications à la mise en œuvre, aux tests, à l’examen du code, à la documentation, au débogage, au déploiement et à la réponse aux incidents.
Identifier et automatiser les activités répétitives ou à faible valeur ajoutée. Prototyper les flux de travail agentic à fort impact et les outils internes, les évaluer en fonction des améliorations mesurables dans la vitesse de livraison, la qualité, la fiabilité et la capacité de l’équipe, pas seulement les taux d’adoption.
Établir des normes pratiques pour l’utilisation responsable de l’IA (sécurité, confidentialité, propriété intellectuelle, qualité, responsabilité). Créer une culture d’expérimentation tout en veillant à ce que les gens restent responsables de l’exactitude et de la sécurité.
Identifier les opportunités d’IA orientées client qui créent une valeur significative et différenciée, distinguant les capacités authentiques des features motivées par la nouveauté. Partenaire avec les clients et l’équipe pour valider et hiérarchiser.
Équilibrer nouvelles fonctionnalités, dette technique, fiabilité et sécurité. Évaluer les compromis avec l’équipe et maintenir des exigences claires de qualité et de confidentialité.

Votre profil

8+ années de leadership en développement logiciel, incluant la construction et la mise à l’échelle d’équipes d’ingénierie.
Expérience pratique en développement logiciel et capacité actuelle à comprendre une base de code, programmer, tester et livrer des fonctionnalités en production.
Expérience de direction d’une équipe de développement, avec responsabilité de la livraison et capacité à recruter, coacher et faire progresser les développeurs.
Solide jugement produit : comprendre les problèmes clients, piloter une feuille de route, prioriser les investissements et mesurer les résultats.
Maîtrise pratique des outils de développement assisté par l’IA et capacité à transmettre des méthodes efficaces, avec validation critique du code généré.
Bonne maîtrise du français et de l’anglais pour collaborer avec les équipes et utiliser la documentation technique.

Notre environnement technologique

Java, Spring, Hibernate, Vue 3, TypeScript, AWS, GitHub Actions et Terraform. Nos applications mobiles fonctionnent hors ligne et se synchronisent. La maîtrise de chaque technologie n’est pas requise.

Nos avantages (et ils valent le détour!)

Chez ProgressionLIVE, on croit que la performance passe par le bien-être.

Voici Ce Qu'on T'offre

Semaine de 4 jours
Télétravail
Assurances collectives après 3 mois (50 % payé par l'entreprise, option famille)
Programme d'aide aux employés (PAE)
Programme de médecine corporative
REER collectif (RPDB)
3 semaines de vacances dès la première année (accessibles après 3 mois)
Activités sociales et sportives régulières
Budget annuel pour de la formation
Budget personnel annuel (équipements sportifs ou de télétravail)
Cafés, collations et bonne humeur garantis au bureau

ProgressionLIVE develops web and mobile software for field service operations, used by hundreds of Canadian organizations across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, construction, transportation, and maintenance.

Your role

Reporting to the General Manager, you will lead the full product and technology team and own the roadmap and delivery. You will jointly agree with the General Manager on product direction, major priorities, and significant investments, while exercising autonomy over day to day product decisions and execution.

You will combine product judgment, team leadership, and direct technical contribution. Your software development experience will enable you to coach developers, build their AI skills, and personally code and ship selected product features. You will draw on the team’s expertise for specialized technical decisions.

Your responsibilities

Own the roadmap, drawing on customer conversations, usage data, and business objectives. Collaborate with sales and customer service, then measure adoption and impact.
Lead execution: define scope, sequence priorities, remove obstacles, and guide the team through release and validation of results.
Personally code and ship selected features, meeting testing, code review, and security standards. Build prototypes and internal tools as needed.
Recruit and develop the team. Coach developers through pair programming, code reviews, training, and knowledge sharing.
Define and lead an AI enabled operating model for product and engineering. Empower developers, QA, and DevOps to use AI effectively across the full development lifecycle, from research and specification through implementation, testing, code review, documentation, debugging, deployment, and incident response.
Identify and automate repetitive or low-value activities. Prototype high-leverage agentic workflows and internal tools, evaluating them based on measurable improvements in delivery speed, quality, reliability, and team capacity, not just adoption rates.
Establish practical standards for responsible AI use (security, privacy, IP, quality, accountability). Build a culture of experimentation while ensuring people remain accountable for correctness and security.
Identify customer-facing AI opportunities that create meaningful, differentiated value, distinguishing genuine capabilities from novelty-driven features. Partner with customers and the team to validate and prioritize.
Balance new capabilities, technical debt, reliability, and security. Evaluate tradeoffs with the team and maintain clear quality and privacy standards.

Our technology environment

Java, Spring, Hibernate, Vue 3, TypeScript, AWS, GitHub Actions, and Terraform. Our mobile applications support offline use and synchronization. Experience with every technology is not required.

Requirements

8+ years of software development leadership, including building and scaling engineering teams.
Practical software development experience and the current ability to understand a codebase, write code, test, and ship production features.
Experience leading a development team, with delivery accountability and the ability to recruit, coach, and develop engineers.
Strong product judgment: understanding customer problems, owning a roadmap, prioritizing investments, and measuring outcomes.
Practical command of AI coding tools and the ability to teach effective methods, including critical review of generated code.
Strong French and English communication skills to collaborate with teams and work with technical documentation..

Benefits

Benefits (And They're Worth It!)

At ProgressionLIVE, we believe that performance comes through well-being.

Here's What We Offer

4-day work week
Remote work
Group insurance after 3 months (50% paid by company, family option)
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Corporate wellness program
Group RRSP (RPDB)
3 weeks vacation from day one (accessible after 3 months)
Regular social and sports activities
Annual training budget
Annual personal budget (sports or remote work equipment)
Coffee, snacks, and good vibes guaranteed at the office

jobs.title: Shopify Practice Director
jobs.description:
Why Valtech? We’re the experience innovation company - a trusted partner to the world’s most recognized brands. To our people we offer growth opportunities, a values-driven culture, international careers and the chance to shape the future of experience.

The opportunity

At Valtech, you’ll find an environment designed for continuous learning, meaningful impact, and professional growth. Whether you're pioneering new digital solutions, challenging conventional thinking or building the next generation of customer experiences, your work will help transform industries.

We Are Proud Of

The work we do and the innovation we drive
Our values of share, care and dare
A workplace culture that fosters creativity, diversity and autonomy
Our borderless, global framework, which enables seamless collaboration

The role

Please note, we are only accepting applicants from the provinces of Ontario and Québec for this role.
For Québec-based candidates, fluency in English is necessary because the position entails collaboration with teams based in the rest of Americas and occasionally in Europe.

As Practice Director, Shopify Commerce, you will own the technical vision, delivery excellence, and business development strategy for our enterprise Shopify Plus practice. You will lead a global team of architects, engineers, and solution consultants—shaping how we design, build, and scale mission-critical commerce platforms for our largest clients. This role sits at the intersection of enterprise commerce architecture, active sales engagement, and talent leadership. You will be expected to command deep, hands-on knowledge of the Shopify Plus ecosystem and the broader technology stack that surrounds it—including ERP integrations, enterprise search, customer data platforms, and headless commerce patterns—and translate that expertise into winning proposals, trusted client partnerships, and a world-class team.

Why Join Us?

Lead a practice at the forefront of enterprise Shopify Plus—working with some of the world’s most ambitious commerce brands.
Collaborate with global experts across strategy, design, engineering, and commerce operations to deliver end-to-end transformation.
Shape how our firm thinks about and delivers Shopify—building playbooks, growing a team, and influencing the direction of a high-growth practice.

Role Responsibilities

Shopify Plus Architecture & Technology Strategy

Define and own the architectural patterns and best practices for enterprise Shopify Plus deployments, including headless/composable commerce, Shopify Functions, Markets Pro, and B2B capabilities.
Lead the design of end-to-end commerce ecosystems spanning Shopify Plus and adjacent enterprise systems—ERP (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite), enterprise search (Elasticsearch, Algolia, Kenshoo), CDP/CRM (Salesforce, Segment, mParticle), PIM, OMS, and payment gateways.
Evaluate and stay ahead of emerging Shopify platform capabilities (e.g., Shopify Audiences, Checkout Extensibility, Editions releases) and translate them into client-ready solutions and internal playbooks.
Serve as the practice’s ultimate authority on technical feasibility, scalability, and integration strategy for Shopify Plus engagements.

Delivery Leadership

Oversee technical delivery across global, cross-functional teams delivering enterprise Shopify Plus solutions, ensuring quality, performance, and client satisfaction at scale.
Establish governance frameworks, risk mitigation strategies, and delivery KPIs tailored to the pace and complexity of commerce platform engagements. -
Act as a technical escalation point and actively unblock delivery teams, modeling the kind of senior leadership and decisiveness the practice requires.
Build, retain, and develop a high-performing team of Shopify architects, engineers, and solution leads—setting clear expectations, creating growth paths, and fostering a culture of technical excellence.

Sales Engagement & Client Partnership

Own the technical narrative in the sales process: participate actively in discovery, solutioning, estimation, architecture design, and proposal development for Shopify Plus pursuits.
Partner closely with business development and account teams to identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities within existing Shopify Plus engagements.
Serve as a credible, senior technical voice in client-facing conversations—building trust, managing expectations, and positioning our practice as a strategic partner, not just a vendor.
Maintain and deepen relationships with Shopify’s partner and alliance teams, ensuring we are positioned for early access to new programs, beta capabilities, and co-sell opportunities.

Practice Development & Talent Growth

Mentor and coach Shopify architects, technical leads, and engineers across regions—actively investing in their growth and career trajectories.
Drive Shopify-specific certification and enablement programs (e.g., Shopify Partner certifications, Shopify Developer certifications) and build learning paths that keep the team at the forefront of platform innovation.
Contribute to internal knowledge sharing, solution playbooks, case studies, and reusable architecture assets that accelerate delivery and sales across the practice.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Utilization Optimization: Maintain or improve team utilization rates across all Shopify Plus engagements, targeting 70%+ blended team utilization.
Certification Growth: Drive 100% of the practice team to hold at least one Shopify Partner or Developer certification within 12 months.
Solution Quality: Ensure architectural integrity, scalability, and maintainability across all delivered Shopify Plus solutions—measured by client satisfaction scores and post-launch performance benchmarks.
Sales Pipeline Contribution: Actively participate in pursuits contributing to at least $8M in unweighted Shopify Commerce pipeline annually, with a target of closing $3M+ in new logos or significant expansions.
Individual Billability: Maintain a minimum of 50% individual billable utilization, balanced against the practice-building and sales activities inherent to this role.
Team Retention & Growth: Achieve 85%+ retention within the practice and maintain a pipeline of at least two internal candidates ready for promotion annually.

Must Have Qualifications

To be considered for this role, you must meet the following essential qualifications:

10+ years of experience in enterprise technology leadership within a consulting, systems integration, or agency environment—with at least 3–4 years specifically in Shopify Plus or a comparable enterprise commerce platform.
Deep, hands-on expertise in the Shopify Plus platform: Shopify Functions, Checkout Extensibility, Markets Pro, B2B, headless/composable commerce architectures, and the Shopify app ecosystem.
Strong command of the enterprise commerce technology stack surrounding Shopify Plus—including ERP integrations (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite), enterprise search (Elasticsearch, Algolia), CDPs (Segment, mParticle, Salesforce Data Cloud), PIM, OMS, and payment platforms.
Proven track record of participating in or leading sales pursuits, proposals, and client-facing solutioning conversations—comfortable owning a technical narrative in a competitive deal.
Experience building, leading, and growing distributed technical teams—hiring, mentoring, retaining senior talent, and creating cultures of technical excellence.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills; able to operate fluently across executive, technical, and commercial audiences.

Preferred Certifications

Shopify Partner Certification, Shopify Developer Certification, or Shopify Plus Certification (required or expected within 6 months of hire).
AWS/Azure/GCP Solutions Architect, TOGAF, SAFe, PMP, or equivalent—demonstrating both platform-level and enterprise architecture credentials.

Commitment to reaching all kinds of people

We design experiences that work for all kinds of people - and that starts with our own teams. At Valtech, we’re intentional about building an inclusive culture where everyone feels supported to grow, thrive and achieve their goals. No matter your background, you belong here. Explore our Diversity & Inclusion site to see how we’re creating a more equitable Valtech for all.

The Benefits

This is a full time position based in Quebec, Canada
.

Valtech offers a comprehensive benefits package effective after three months of continuous service:

A comprehensive insurance plan, where you can choose the module that best suits your needs—Gold, Silver, or Bronze. The employer may contribute up to 80% of your coverage depending on the selected module. This plan includes short- and long-term disability coverage.
Dialogue via Sun Life provides virtual healthcare services, allowing you to consult with a healthcare professional for emergencies, prescription renewals, and more. You also have access to the Employee and Family Assistance Program, as well as a complete mental health support program.
A $500 Personal Spending Account, which can be used for healthcare reimbursements, gym memberships, public transit passes, office supplies, or contributions to your RRSP through Valtech.
A retirement plan where Valtech will match 100% of your RRSP contributions through a Deferred Profit Sharing Plan (DPSP), up to a maximum of 4%. You can start contributing to your RRSP immediately, and to the DPSP after 3 months. The vesting of the DPSP will be after a 24 months of service.
Access to a flexible vacation under Valtech's policy to support your work-life balance, with 5 days available during your probation period and a prorated amount calculated for the remainder of the year.
Personal Technology Reimbursement – $30/month for every employee-offered on day 1.
We close during the winter holidays and offer flexible scheduling throughout the year, so you can enjoy those sunny Friday afternoons—provided your weekly hours are completed.

Your application process

Once you apply, our Talent Acquisition team will review your application. If your skills and experience align with the role, we’ll reach out for next steps. Your CV should cover key information on relevant experiences and expertise. We do not require information such as age, gender, marital status, or a headshot in your application. We review all candidates based on skills, experience, and potential.

⚠️ Beware of recruitment fraud: Only engage with official Valtech email addresses.

We are committed to inclusion and accessibility. If you need reasonable accommodations during the interview process, please either indicate it in your application or let your Talent Partner know.

About Valtech

Valtech is the experience innovation company that exists to unlock a better way to experience the world. By blending crafts, categories, and cultures, we help brands unlock new value in an increasingly digital world.

At the intersection of data, AI, creativity, and technology, we drive transformation for leading organizations, including L’Oréal, Mars, Audi, P&G, Volkswagen Dolby, and more.

At Valtech, we don’t just talk about transformation. We make it happen. Our people are the heart of our success, and we foster a workplace where everyone has the support to thrive, grow and innovate.

Are you ready to create what’s next? Join us.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Product Management, Endpoint Security and XDR
jobs.description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role:

Elastic Security is hiring a Senior Director of Product Management to lead our Endpoint Security & XDR business. This role reports to the GM of Elastic Security. You will be paired with our most senior engineering leader, a VP who leads all of Elastic Security engineering and whose day-to-day focus is endpoint, sharing accountability for the line's outcomes with you. You will also peer with the product lead of our SIEM and analytics business as we build one platform together. The endpoint is where we meet the adversary directly, and where the people we serve, the analysts and defenders protecting hospitals, banks, and government networks, need us most. Their mission is our mission, and this role carries that responsibility for the endpoint and XDR market. Like Elastic itself, the role is distributed by design.

This business was born when Elastic acquired Endgame in 2019, a pioneer in endpoint prevention, detection, and response with roots in defending national security networks. We extended that protection philosophy to Linux and cloud-native environments with the Cmd acquisition in 2021. The result today is Elastic Defend, and its record in independent testing reflects the quality of the work: Elastic Security was the only vendor to score 100% protection in both the AV-Comparatives Real-World and Malware Protection Tests for all of 2025, and the only vendor among 16 to earn a perfect malware protection score in the 2026 Business Security Test, with zero false alarms on the software businesses actually run. And unlike most of this market, we do that work in the open: our protection artifacts and detection rules are public for anyone to inspect.

This role is open for a straightforward reason. Our product leader is retiring, and we are organizing product management around our two core businesses: SIEM and analytics, which will be led by a proven leader already at Elastic, and endpoint, where we are looking outside for someone who brings a fresh perspective from this market. The timing is deliberate in another way as well: security operations are shifting toward agentic workflows, and as a challenger in this market we can move faster than the incumbents. Our focus with this role is business expertise: we are looking for a business owner who understands endpoint security deeply and who will grow this line with the care of someone who owns the outcome. You will have genuine room to lead. The strategy, the priorities, and how we compete are yours to shape with your engineering partner.

What You Will Be Doing:

Drive the business-driven OKRs for the Endpoint Security & XDR line: revenue contribution, competitive win rate, platform attach, retention, and expansion.
Set the product strategy for the line and represent it with sales leadership, customers, and analysts: a clear diagnosis of the market, a guiding policy, and coherent actions that follow from it.
Own the agentic detection and response strategy for the endpoint: where AI-driven and autonomous capabilities genuinely help prevention, detection, and response at the edge, working closely with the SIEM and analytics line so customers experience one agentic platform, not two roadmaps.
Shape where we invest and where we choose not to, building the case with data and customer evidence.
Own how endpoint and XDR fit the broader Elastic Security platform story, so a customer who lands with endpoint expands into the platform and a SIEM customer sees why our endpoint belongs next to it.
Put customers first. Visit them where they are, participate in deals and win/loss reviews, enable the field, and represent Elastic at tradeshows and industry events. This work requires regular travel.
Partner with your engineering counterpart as a true pair, sharing one set of outcomes for the line.
Lead and develop a team of product managers, helping each of them connect their work to the customer's mission and the business.

What You Bring:

Genuine care for the people this product protects. Customers can tell whether the person across the table is invested in their mission, and this business runs on the trust you earn by caring consistently over time.
Business expertise running a product line or business unit in security, with comfort in the full picture: revenue, win rates, retention, pricing and packaging, and competitive positioning.
Earned credibility in endpoint security: EPP, EDR, XDR, and enough understanding of what an agent does on a machine to have real conversations with engineers and practitioners.
A strong working partnership with go-to-market teams, including experience enabling sellers and supporting deals alongside the field.
A habit of deciding with evidence: win/loss data, customer conversations, and market signals inform your calls.
A point of view on how a challenger competes and differentiates against well-funded incumbents.
Clear executive communication with executive leadership, CISOs, sales leadership, and industry analysts.

Bonus Points:

Experience competing with or working at endpoint-focused security vendors, with perspective on the strengths and gaps across the market.
Experience helping a security business scale from a few hundred million toward $1B.
Familiarity with public efficacy testing (AV-Comparatives, MITRE ATT&CK evaluations) and how to participate in the open.
Experience serving customers in hard environments: regulated industries, classified networks, air-gapped and OT deployments.
A thoughtful position on AI and agentic capabilities at the endpoint, with healthy skepticism of silver bullets and a clear sense of where they genuinely help the defender.
Contributions to open source or the security community. Our work is public, and we value people who build in the open.

Additional Information - We Take Care of Our People:

As a distributed company, diversity drives our identity. Whether you’re looking to launch a new career or grow an existing one, Elastic is the type of company where you can balance great work with great life. Your age is only a number. It doesn’t matter if you’re just out of college or your children are; we need you for what you can do.

We strive to have parity of benefits across regions, and while regulations differ from place to place, we believe taking care of our people is the right thing to do.

Competitive pay based on the work you do here and not your previous salary
Health coverage for you and your family in many locations
Ability to craft your calendar with flexible locations and schedules for many roles
Generous number of vacation days each year
Increase your impact - We match up to $2000 (or local currency equivalent) for financial donations and service
Up to 40 hours each year to use toward volunteer projects you love
Embracing parenthood with a minimum of 16 weeks of parental leave

Security & Privacy Responsibilities:
Take ownership of protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of organizational data and systems by following applicable privacy and security policies, standards, and procedures. Ensure that all individual contributions follow Elastic’s Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF). Proactively participate in mandatory role-based training to ensure personal technical execution consistently aligns with the highest standards of data protection, data privacy, and system resilience.

jobs.title: Head of People & Culture (12 month contract)

Description

Resolver operates as a hybrid workforce with a mix of both at home and in office work. For this particular role we are looking for someone who wants to be with us in person 2-3 times per week.

As our Head of People and Culture (HR), you’ll lead the global People function supporting approximately 350 Resolverites. You’ll work closely with our executive team to turn business priorities into practical plans that strengthen leadership, retain great talent and help our organization navigate change.

You’ll lead a small team across Talent Acquisition, Business Partnering, Talent and Leadership, and People Operations. About Resolver:

Resolver is a high-growth SaaS company whose intuitive, no-code platform gives our customers a clear picture of their risks so they can make quick and effective decisions. As a part of the Resolver team, your work will help transform risk management to risk intelligence so organizations can protect people and assets and deliver on their purpose.

We are ambitious in both our mission and our culture. As a business within Kroll, we offer an innovative, non-hierarchical work environment blended with the stability and financial security of an enterprise. Resolver has also been named one of Canada’s Great Places to Work six years in a row!

Talent Strategy & Organizational Design

Measures of Success:
Delivery of People priorities; workforce plans aligned to business needs and budget; clear accountabilities following organization changes; credibility with executives as an independent People leader.

Co-create talent strategy and translate agreed business and talent priorities into an annual People plan. Own execution of quarterly deliverables, resource decisions and measures of success. Recommend changes as business needs evolve.
Advise executives and senior leaders on organizational effectiveness, workforce decisions, retention and sensitive employee matters. Challenge assumptions and recommend commercially sound actions.
Lead the People contribution to organization design with executives, clarifying accountabilities, decision rights, reporting relationships and capability needs. Evaluate cost and delivery implications with our Finance partners.

Transformation and Organizational Change

Measures of Success:
Adoption of priority changes against agreed milestones; manager and employee readiness; demonstrated application of new skills; measurable AI improvements in capacity or quality with effective safeguards

Enable a mindset of transformation and business resilience by helping leaders anticipate change, challenge established ways of working and build the capabilities and adaptability needed to sustain performance.
Lead the People workstream for business AI enablement. Collaborate to assess how work, roles and skills should change, then build workforce, reskilling and manager enablement plans.
Own the People approach to transformation, from impact and readiness assessments to manager preparation, employee communications and adoption measures. Personally lead the most complex changes.
Apply AI within People processes through focused pilots. Establish baselines and measure time saved, service quality and adoption before scaling. Use approved tools and agreed data safeguards, with human review of consequential decisions.

Talent Management and Leadership Enablement

Measures of Success:
Retention of top performers and critical talent; succession readiness and internal progression; stronger manager effectiveness; employee understanding of key priorities and changes; timely compensation reviews within budget and agreed pay parameters.

Oversee talent management programs: performance management, talent reviews, succession planning and career development. Turn assessments into specific development and retention actions for top performers and critical roles.
Set the leadership development agenda around business needs. Equip managers to coach, give feedback, manage performance and lead change. Hold leaders accountable for applying these practices.
Oversee engagement and employee communications through the Talent and Leadership Partner. Use employee feedback and exit insights to improve leadership practices and the employee experience
Oversee compensation practices and annual review delivery, including market positioning, salary structures, promotions and pay decisions within approved budgets.

Business Partnering

Measures of Success:
Senior leader confidence in People advice; timely, well-documented resolution of complex cases; completion of agreed manager actions; appropriate escalation of material risks. .

Oversee Business Partnering across functions and countries. Ensure consistent advice while accounting for local context.
Directly support senior leaders and complex changes, balancing business objectives, employee impact and People risk.
Lead complex employee relations and performance cases, using specialist advice where needed. Apply sound judgment, maintain appropriate documentation and resolve issues promptly.
Build the Business Partner’s capability and establish clear escalation boundaries.

Talent Acquisition

Measures of Success:
Priority roles filled against agreed plans; time to fill and offer acceptance; quality of hire assessed through early performance and retention; consistent hiring manager participation and candidate experience.

Oversee recruiting outcomes against approved workforce plans, ensuring alignment on hiring priorities and capacity.
Partner with the Talent Acquisition team to improve assessment quality and hiring manager discipline

HR Operations

Measures of Success:
Accurate and timely payroll inputs and employee records; headcount and workforce costs reconciled with Finance; timely employee service; workforce insights that inform decisions and track results; completion of risk mitigations and remediation against agreed deadlines.

Oversee benefits, HR systems, employee records, policies and lifecycle administration.
Ensure reliable service and accurate People reporting across countries.
Coordinate local employment requirements through appropriate advisers and providers. Maintain confidentiality, data quality and operational backup, with particular attention to Canada and India.
Own the People analytics agenda, with consistent metric definitions and reliable reporting on headcount, workforce costs, hiring, retention, performance and succession. Reconcile core data with Finance and establish reporting appropriate to each audience.
Turn workforce data into actionable insights. Identify patterns by function, geography and critical talent group, distinguish underlying causes from symptoms, and recommend actions. Track whether interventions improve outcomes while protecting employee confidentiality.
Own the identification and management of People risks, including employment practices, employee relations, compensation, data privacy and continuity of critical roles and HR services. Maintain a prioritized risk register with clear owners, mitigation actions and escalation thresholds.
Oversee compliance with applicable employment requirements across operating countries, working with Legal and local advisers to keep policies, records and controls current. Partner with Finance and Technology on related controls. Review recurring gaps, coordinate remediation and maintain documentation that supports audits and diligence.

Team Leadership and Operational Effectiveness

Delivery of team commitments and individual development plans; team engagement scores.

Lead the entire People team, setting priorities, performance expectations and development plans. Resolve capacity constraints and remain directly involved in delivery when complexity or workload requires it.
Coach and develop the team to a high standard of performance, with regular feedback and clear accountability for results.
Own the People budget, vendor performance and team performance scorecard. Simplify processes and improve handoffs, system use and service effectiveness with the team.

What you will bring:

You have built your People career over the last 10 or more years, with experience leading a broad function and developing a team. Whether your education was in HR, business or a related field, you have the depth to oversee Talent Management, Talent Acquisition, HR Operations, Compensation and Business Partnering. A CHRL or relevant designation is an asset.
You are a People leader with strong business acumen. You understand how workforce choices affect cost, capability and performance, and you are comfortable advising and challenging executives. You have the judgment and credibility to own the function independently and know when a decision warrants escalation.
You know how to turn strategy into reality. You have delivered organization design and change initiatives across functions or geographies, and you stay close to implementation. You help leaders navigate uncertainty, build resilience and sustain new ways of working.
You have proven success in building a strong employee experience and translating culture into everyday leadership practices. What We’ll Give You In Return

Resolver is one of Canada's Great Workplaces. Culture isn't just something we write about (although we do), we live our values and challenge each other to be our best selves. .

What we are looking for

Reporting to the Chief Legal & Policy Officer, the Vice President, Compliance, Privacy and Bank of Canada Affairs is a senior-level executive and advisor to Payments Canada’s Executive Leadership Team on all matters related to compliance, privacy and the regulatory oversight relationship with the Bank of Canada.

Responsibilities Of The Position Include

Compliance Mandate: Oversee Payments Canada’s compliance with laws and regulatory requirements to maintain legal compliance and uphold integrity.
Privacy Mandate: Act as the designated Chief Privacy Officer for Payments Canada, accountable for compliance with privacy laws and regulations and for Payments Canada’s privacy management program.
Bank of Canada Affairs Mandate: Responsible and accountable for managing the oversight relationship with the Bank of Canada, for the observance of the Bank of Canada risk-management standards for our designated payment systems, and Payments Canada’s obligations with regard to the Bank of Canada Oversight Agreement.

Duties And Responsibilities

Compliance

Manage the corporate compliance function, exercising specialized knowledge of business processes, regulatory and corporate compliance requirements.
Maintain effective relationships with Payments Canada’s regulators, including the Bank of Canada and Department of Finance, in cooperation with the Government Relations team, to support Payments Canada’s regulatory compliance obligations under the Canadian Payments Act and Payment Clearing and Settlement Act.
Develop, implement and maintain up to date an enterprise regulatory compliance management program, including systems, policies, procedures, structures and internal controls to ensure compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations.
Develop the annual work plan (compliance, privacy and Bank of Canada Affairs) considering Payments Canada’s strategic objectives and risk profile; and periodically revising the plan in light of ongoing developments.
Provide reasonable assurance to senior management and the Board that there are effective and efficient policies and procedures in place, well understood and respected by all employees and that Payments Canada is in compliance with regulatory requirements.
Foster a culture of ethics throughout the organization, promoting awareness and understanding of compliance requirements and expectations.
Promote compliance input and leadership to business partners across the organization, including Human Resources, Legal, Payment Operations, Payment Products, Security, Risk and Policy.
Partner with business units to ensure compliance obligations are considered and integrated into new products or initiatives.
Report to the Board annually on the general state of regulatory and corporate compliance.
Oversee the implementation and maintenance of the corporate policy framework for compliance-related responsibilities and topics.
Provide input and guidance on corporate policy framework and training programs to support and educate employees on compliance-related responsibilities and topics.
Act as designated recipient of anonymous complaints under Payments Canada’s Code of Conduct and Respect and Safety in the Work Place policy and work with Legal and Human Resources teams to assess and resolve complaints and issues, including conflicts of interest, raised by employees in relation to the Code of Conduct or Respect and Safety in the Work Place policy.
Review and provide recommendations to the President and CEO regarding enterprise compliance complaints.
Oversee the annual process for business unit confirmation of compliance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements.

Privacy

Act as the designated individual, Chief Privacy Officer (required by privacy legislation) accountable for compliance with privacy laws and regulations.
Develop and maintain Payments Canada’s privacy management program.
Implement strategies, policies and procedures to protect personal information in Payments Canada’s possession or custody, including conducting privacy impact assessments, when applicable.
Provide privacy related advice for the selection, development and implementation of new technological solutions, programs, projects and related processes.
Review and sign off on requests for information under the Access to Information Act.
Establish procedures to record and report breaches involving personal information, and respond to security breaches, complaints and inquiries.
Report and notify individuals in the event of a privacy breach.
Ensure training on privacy procedures and policies, and communication to employees on Payments Canada’s policies and procedures.

Bank of Canada Affairs

Manage the institutional regulatory oversight relationship with the Bank of Canada, including regular engagement with the Bank of Canada Oversight team to keep the Bank of Canada informed on the delivery of regulatory priorities, core assurance review progress and findings and initiatives involving significant changes to Payments Canada’s systems and operations.
Responsible and accountable for the enterprise observance of the Bank of Canada risk-management standards for our designated payment systems, associated guidelines and Payments Canada’s statutory obligations with regard to the Bank of Canada’s Oversight Agreement.
Enterprise primary point of contact for the Bank of Canada’s oversight function.

Oversee reporting of the execution of regulatory initiatives and priorities with a focus on quality and timeliness.
Review and provide input on annual system self-assessments, including seeking approval of self-assessments by the Board.
Facilitate the execution of the Bank’s core assurance reviews, including coordinating the review, submission processes, reviewing materials, providing advice and guidance to teams, liaising with business partners and the Bank.

Develop, implement and maintain a divisional strategy in line with the organizational strategy, designed to enhance or reliably sustain existing services over the longer term, and to proactively identify opportunities for new or amended services.
Attract and retain professionals with the skill sets and competencies needed to deliver Payments Canada’s strategic priorities.

Responsible and accountable for all aspects of the talent management cycle (i.e., workforce planning, recruitment, performance management, staff development, succession planning) for the team, including developing group and individual development plans for team members to support a culture of continuous learning and development.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Ontario Plants Propagation (OP) is a leading North American plant propagation company focused on producing high-quality young vegetable and soft fruit plants for commercial greenhouse growers. As a critical supplier to the controlled environment agriculture sector, OP combines horticultural expertise, advanced growing capabilities, and a commitment to innovation to support a more resilient, productive, and sustainable food system.

Following the development of its state-of-the-art Glencoe greenhouse facility and significant capital investment, OP is entering an exciting next phase of growth and transformation. The organization is focused on optimizing operations, enhancing profitability, expanding capabilities, and strengthening its position in a market benefiting from growing demand for greenhouse-grown food production.

The Mandate

Reporting directly to the CEO and working closely with ownership, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) will play a central role in helping build a high-performing, scalable, and profitable organization. This is not a traditional finance leadership position focused solely on stewardship and reporting. It is an opportunity to become a true business partner and strategic leader, influencing critical decisions that will shape the future of the company.

The successful candidate will join at a pivotal point in OP's evolution. With substantial investments already made in infrastructure and growth, the organization is seeking a finance leader who can help unlock value by improving profitability, strengthening cash generation, enhancing decision-making capabilities, and building the financial and operational foundations needed to support long-term success.

For an executive who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, building capabilities, and creating lasting impact, this role offers a rare opportunity to influence strategy, strengthen culture, enhance performance, and leave a visible mark on a growing business.

Leadership and Stewardship

The company is seeking a CFO who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. More than just a technical financial leader, the successful candidate will be a thoughtful and credible executive who fosters trust, accountability, and collaboration across the organization and partners effectively with external stakeholders.
Operationally curious and highly intelligent, with a low-ego leadership style
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and complexity
A builder of high-performing teams and organizational culture
Results-oriented and accountable
An enabler of exceptional data-driven decision making
Collaborative, trusted, and relationship-focused
Energized by operational challenges and continuous improvement
An effective and transparent communicator

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will be a strategic and operational finance executive who enjoys complexity and thrives in a growth-oriented environment. They will bring both financial expertise and a passion for helping businesses improve performance and create value.
CPA designation required.
Proven track record of success as a CFO or senior finance executive within a complex operating environment with a minimum of 15 years, including optimizing and scaling organizations
Accomplished as a strategic business partner, advisor to the CEO and the senior leadership team
Hands-on and strategic capabilities in financial planning, forecasting, cash flow management, and business intelligence, driving operational improvements through financial insights and performance management.
Experience operating in asset-intensive, capital-intensive, or leveraged environments.
Track record of building high-performing teams and influencing leaders across an organization.
Experience in manufacturing, food production, agriculture, horticulture, or other operationally intensive industries is strongly preferred.
Experience working with sophisticated lenders, private equity sponsors, family offices, or institutional investors is also an asset.

Location

Strengthening accountability by designing and improving frameworks, performance measures and monitoring approaches for physician remuneration models and funded initiatives.

jobs.description:
About The Role

We are seeking an experienced and collaborative leader to join H&R Block Canada as Interim Director, Products & Services for a 12-month term. The Interim Director will provide leadership and continuity for the Associate Products & Services portfolio, working with an established team of Product Management professionals to maintain focus, coordination, and delivery against established priorities.

This role is well suited to a leader who can quickly build an understanding of the portfolio, work effectively through subject-matter experts, and provide clear direction and oversight. The Interim Director will support the team in advancing product and service priorities while engaging cross-functional partners and senior leaders as appropriate. This position is based in Calgary and offers a hybrid work schedule, with 3 days per week in-office.

Reporting Structure and Team

Reporting to the Vice President, Products & Services, the Interim Director provides leadership to a team of Product Management professionals across senior product management, product management, associate product management, and digital product management roles. The Interim Director will work closely with these experienced team members, provide direction and support, remove barriers, and escalate matters as appropriate.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Leadership and Team Support

Provide day-to-day leadership and continuity for the team throughout the 12-month term.
Build an understanding of current priorities, products, stakeholders, and ways of working through a structured transition and ongoing partnership with the team.
Set clear expectations, support decision-making, hold regular check-ins, and help team members remain aligned on priorities and commitments.
Coach and support direct reports while drawing on their expertise in product management, UX, technology, and other relevant functional areas.
Create an environment where issues are raised early and work with the team and senior leaders to resolve issues and identify practical solutions.

Oversight of Products and Services

Oversee progress against established product and service plans, including priorities related to small business, specialty tax, Block Pro, Core/CIS, and digital products.
Work with Product Managers to review roadmaps, milestones, risks, dependencies, and launch readiness while maintaining appropriate accountability for delivery.
Support the team in maintaining oversight of product performance, budgets, client impacts, and field operational considerations.
Help ensure recommendations and decisions are supported by available data, client feedback, and the expertise of responsible team members.
Maintain awareness of financial services work within the portfolio and engage subject-matter experts and senior leaders when specialized guidance or approvals are required.

Cross-Functional Coordination

Coordinate with internal partners to maintain momentum on agreed priorities and clarify roles, timelines, and decision points.
Facilitate collaboration among Product Management, UX Design & Content Strategy, technology, operations, delivery services and PMG, marketing, finance, and other stakeholders as required.
Provide clear updates to senior leadership on progress, risks, resource needs, and decisions requiring additional support.
Maintain existing third-party and vendor relationships in partnership with the appropriate internal owners, escalating material issues as required.
Support existing Tax Pro and franchisee focus groups and manage feedback and escalations relating to Associate products.

Continuity and Transition

Maintain continuity of key processes, meetings, reporting, and stakeholder relationships throughout the 12-month term.
Document significant decisions, open items, risks, and status updates to support an effective transition at the conclusion of the term.
Exercise sound judgment by identifying situations that require specialized expertise or senior-level guidance and seeking appropriate support to mitigate risk and enable informed decision-making.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree; MBA would be an asset.
Significant leadership experience in product management, financial services, eCommerce, retail, software, digital products, or a related environment.
People-leadership experience, including the ability to set expectations, coach team members, address barriers, and support accountability.
Experience leading cross-functional teams and coordinating work across multiple priorities and stakeholders.
Ability to quickly learn new subject matter, ask appropriate questions, and engage technical and functional experts when making or escalating decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

Comfort reviewing plans, status updates, risks, budgets, financial results, and performance information to support informed decisions.
Strong communication, facilitation, organization, and relationship-management skills.
Proven ability to establish priorities, meet deadlines, and make timely, data-informed decisions.
Ability to lead effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment.

Why work for us

For over 60 years, H&R Block has prepared taxes for millions of Canadians annually. Headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, we serve taxpayers in more than 1,000+ offices, through our upload from home service, and online with our DIY tax software. Our dedicated team of Tax Experts use the latest in electronic processing and filing technology to prepare all types of returns, including personal, small business, corporate, farm, trucker, fishing, U.S., rental, and estate.

Becoming an H&R Block Associate is an opportunity to grow with the strongest brand in the tax preparation industry. We are looking for people who want to provide help and inspire confidence in our clients and communities. We know that the ability to deliver outstanding client service starts with having the best talent on our team, and if you want to be part of our success story then we want to hear from you!

We offer competitive base wages and targeted incentive opportunities, a generous benefits package with options for health care spending or wellness resources, RRSP Matching, Employee Stock Programs, and Block “Wellness Days” to encourage rest outside of Tax Season.

Proof of legal authorization to work in Canada will be required as part of the recruitment process. Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

helping drive positive change in emerging markets?

We are looking for a Director, Climate Mobilization
!

Join FinDev Canada, Canada's development financial institution! We work with and through the private sector to advance climate and nature action, gender equality, and market development in emerging markets and developing economies. Joining FinDev means being part of a growing, purpose-driven organization where your expertise directly contributes to meaningful, measurable impact around the world.

FinDev Canada is at a pivotal moment in its evolution. As we expand our climate ambitions and strengthen our focus on mobilizing private capital at scale, we are building new capabilities to identify, develop, and accelerate transformative climate investment opportunities across emerging markets.

This is more than a leadership role. It is an opportunity to build and lead a new strategic capability at FinDev Canada at a time when climate finance and private capital mobilization are central to our future ambitions. The successful candidate will help shape how FinDev Canada engages with global investors and partners, develops innovative climate investment opportunities, and mobilizes capital toward meaningful climate outcomes across emerging markets.

As Director, Climate Mobilization, you will help define and execute a critical institutional priority, build a new team from the ground up, and position FinDev Canada as a partner of choice for leading investors, fund managers, development finance institutions, and other climate finance stakeholders. Few roles offer the opportunity to influence strategy, build a platform, and create impact at this scale.

Employment Type:
Fixed Term Contract for 2 years or Temporary Assignment (for internal applicants)

Location:
FinDev Canada headquarters is in downtown Montreal. For the right candidate, Ottawa or Toronto will be considered, with the flexibility to work under a hybrid model, with a current requirement of three in-office days per week (subject to change).

Director - Investments 21: Salaries typically range from $150,715 - $226,073 annually, based on qualifications and experiences

Why You'll Love Working Here

Impactful Work: We are driven by our mandate to promote sustainable and inclusive growth in emerging markets and developing economies. Every role contributes to creating positive, lasting impact - for our clients, the markets we serve, and communities around the world.
Inspiring Colleagues: Join a diverse and talented team from around the world that brings a wealth of experience, knowledge, and passion to everything we do. We believe strong results come from strong partnerships - working together, sharing perspectives, and building trust to achieve shared goals.

The Climate Mobilization Team (CMT) has been established as a strategic initiative reporting directly to the Chief Investment Officer. Created to support delivery of FinDev Canada's Climate Mobilization Strategy, the team focuses on identifying, originating, and advancing transformative climate investment opportunities that require dedicated partnership development, market creation, and mobilization expertise before they become investment-ready.

Working closely with investment teams, institutional investors, fund managers, governments, and other strategic partners, the team plays a critical role in building FinDev Canada's climate pipeline, accelerating private capital mobilization, and translating climate ambition into investable opportunities and measurable impact. As a newly established function, the team offers a unique opportunity to help shape how FinDev Canada delivers on its climate objectives in the years ahead.

What You Will Be Doing

Build, lead, and develop FinDev Canada's Climate Mobilization Team.
Lead the execution and evolution of FinDev Canada's Climate Mobilization Strategy and climate opportunity pipeline.
Identify, develop, and advance high-potential climate investment opportunities and partnerships.
Shape opportunities from early-stage concepts through investment readiness.
Build and manage relationships with investors, DFIs, governments, fund managers, and other strategic partners.
Develop strategic platforms and partnerships that accelerate climate investment and unlock new market opportunities.
Represent FinDev Canada externally and position the organization as a trusted climate finance partner.
Mobilize private capital toward climate solutions across emerging markets.
Collaborate across investment, blended finance, impact, risk, legal, and strategy teams.
Provide strategic advice to senior leadership on climate mobilization opportunities and market trends.
Strengthen FinDev Canada's institutional capabilities and thought leadership in climate mobilisation.

What We Are Looking For

Master's degree in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, International Development, Public Policy, or a related field.
Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in climate finance, infrastructure finance, development finance, investment banking, private capital mobilisation, blended finance, or related fields.
Significant experience originating, structuring, or developing complex investment opportunities and strategic partnerships in emerging and developing markets.
Demonstrated experience leading senior stakeholder relationships across public, private, and multilateral sectors.
Strong understanding of climate finance, sustainable investment, capital mobilisation, and development impact.
Proven track record leading high-performing teams and delivering strategic initiatives.
Experience working across multiple functions and influencing senior stakeholders in complex organizational environments.
Bilingual in both official languages (English and French)

What Will Make You Stand Out

Experience within a Development Finance Institution (DFI), Multilateral Development Bank (MDB), impact investor, climate-focused fund manager, or international financial institution.
Deep network across climate finance, institutional investors, sovereign entities, foundations, and development finance partners.
Experience establishing new business lines, platforms, or strategic initiatives.
Experience working across emerging markets and developing economies.
Additional language capabilities, particularly Spanish

37.5

Business Management, Strategy & Support

$165,000 - $175,000 CAD

Job Description

Role Overview

The VP, Debt Capital Markets plays a critical role in originating, structuring, and executing debt financing transactions for investment grade clients. Partnering closely with investment banking relationship teams, corporate banking, syndication and sales & trading, the VP advises clients on capital structure, funding strategy, market conditions, and liability management opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

Lead day‑to‑day execution of investment grade debt transactions, overseeing financial modeling, debt capacity analysis, market comparables, and investor materials.
Develop and maintain senior client relationships with CFOs, Treasurers, and other corporate decision-makers, serving as a strategic advisor on capital structure, market conditions, and financing alternatives.
Support structuring of complex financing solutions across sectors.
Manage cross‑functional coordination with syndicate desks, legal counsel, rating agencies, risk teams, and sales & trading.
Provide strategic advice on financing alternatives, capital markets trends, and funding optimization.
Coordinate transaction execution across internal stakeholders, external counsel, rating agencies, and investors.
Prepare client presentations, market updates, and financing recommendations.
Mentor and develop analysts and associates, contributing to professional growth.
Uphold risk management, compliance, and governance standards throughout all deal processes.

Qualifications

5+ years of investment banking or capital markets experience, preferably with exposure to DCM products.
Strong understanding of debt products, capital markets dynamics, and credit analysis.
Demonstrated client management and transaction execution capabilities.
Series 7 and 79 licenses, or the ability to obtain required licenses within the applicable period.
Undergraduate degree required; MBA, CFA, or other relevant professional designation preferred.

Who We Are

TD Securities offers a wide range of capital markets products and services to corporate, government, and institutional clients who choose us for our innovation, execution, and experience. With more than 6,500 professionals operating out of 40 cities across the globe, we strive to make every interaction, product and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple. Our services include underwriting and distributing new issues, providing trusted advice and industry-leading insight, extending access to global markets, and delivering integrated transaction banking solutions. In 2023, we acquired Cowen Inc., offering our clients access to a premier U.S. equities business and highly-diverse equity research franchise, while growing our strong, diversified investment bank.

Together, we are reimagining what banking can be for our clients, colleagues and communities.

Our Total Rewards Package

Our Total Rewards package reflects the investments we make in our colleagues to help them and their families achieve their financial, physical, and mental well-being goals. Total Rewards at TD includes a base salary, variable compensation, and several other key plans such as health and well-being benefits, savings and retirement programs, paid time off, banking benefits and discounts, career development, and reward and recognition programs. Privacy Mandate: Act as the designated Chief Privacy Officer for Payments Canada, accountable for compliance with privacy laws and regulations and for Payments Canada’s privacy management program.

Duties And Responsibilities

Compliance

Develop, implement and maintain up to date an enterprise regulatory compliance management program, including systems, policies, procedures, structures and internal controls to ensure compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations.

Partner with business units to ensure compliance obligations are considered and integrated into new products or initiatives.

Oversee the implementation and maintenance of the corporate policy framework for compliance-related responsibilities and topics.
Provide input and guidance on corporate policy framework and training programs to support and educate employees on compliance-related responsibilities and topics.

Review and provide recommendations to the President and CEO regarding enterprise compliance complaints.
Oversee the annual process for business unit confirmation of compliance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements.

Privacy

Act as the designated individual, Chief Privacy Officer (required by privacy legislation) accountable for compliance with privacy laws and regulations.
Develop and maintain Payments Canada’s privacy management program.
Implement strategies, policies and procedures to protect personal information in Payments Canada’s possession or custody, including conducting privacy impact assessments, when applicable.
Provide privacy related advice for the selection, development and implementation of new technological solutions, programs, projects and related processes.
Review and sign off on requests for information under the Access to Information Act.
Establish procedures to record and report breaches involving personal information, and respond to security breaches, complaints and inquiries.
Report and notify individuals in the event of a privacy breach.
Ensure training on privacy procedures and policies, and communication to employees on Payments Canada’s policies and procedures.
